title: Intrinsic Gradient Barriers in Pushforward Deep Generative Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.34484v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Broad classes of deep generative models (DGMs) operate by learning to map a simple source distribution, such as a standard Gaussian, to a complex high-dimensional target distribution. Despite their success, DGMs often empirically struggle to accurately represent distributions with heavy tails or well-separated modes. In this work, we show that these difficulties reflect intrinsic properties of the underlying transport problem rather than particular neural network architectures or training procedures. We establish quantitative lower bounds on the gradients and Jacobians of pushforward mappings that transport log-concave source distributions to such targets. For heavy-tailed target distributions, the required gradient magnitude grows as the target develops increasingly large moments. For multimodal target distributions, the low-probability regions between well-separated modes similarly force large gradients in the transport map. We discuss

translated_title: 前推深度生成模型中的内在梯度障碍
translated_abstract: 许多类型的深度生成模型（DGMs）通过学习将简单的源分布（如标准高斯分布）映射到复杂的高维目标分布来运行。尽管取得了成功，深度生成模型在经验上往往难以准确表示重尾分布或峰间距较大的多峰分布。在这项工作中，我们证明了这些困难反映的是底层传输问题的内在属性，而非特定的神经网络架构或训练过程。我们对将对数凹源分布传输到此类目标分布的前推映射的梯度和雅可比矩阵建立了定量下界。对于重尾目标分布，所需的梯度幅值会随着目标分布矩的增大而增长。对于多峰目标分布，分离良好的模式之间的低概率区域同样会迫使传输映射中产生大梯度。我们讨论……
tldr: 本文证明了深度生成模型在表示重尾和多峰分布时的困难源于传输问题本身的内在属性而非模型架构或训练方法，并对前推映射的梯度和雅可比矩阵建立了定量下界。
en_tdlr: This paper shows that the difficulty of deep generative models in representing heavy-tailed and multimodal distributions stems from intrinsic properties of the transport problem rather than architectures or training procedures, establishing quantitative lower bounds on the gradients and Jacobians of pushforward mappings.
